## How to write each entry

1. The bold title states the decision or the fact in plain words, no broader than the body.
2. Then its scope and its exact conditions. Keep every condition, exception and limit. A shorter sentence must not lose one.
3. For a position, the reason after "Why:", only if the curator gave one or accepted it in the question, or a finding in `findings.md` gives it with its ground in the team's texts, library or code. For a fact, its evidence: the test, measurement, source reading or report section, and whether it was observed, read in the code or inferred.
4. Keep the state apart: "Built.", or "Still to build:" in one line with where the work is tracked. Keep such lines as they are; do not move them out.
5. Name each thing. Say which call, which checker, which library, which path, when a sentence has two of them. Use no handle of a past conversation or batch ("answer 9", "ask 3", "item 48", "rung C", "decision E") unless a skill defines it.
6. **Pointers.** For each pointer (another entry, a gap-ledger row, a PLAN item, a report), decide first whether it belongs in the entry. If it stays, give it a few words on what it holds, so that a reader can decide whether to follow it without loading it. If it is only provenance, move it to the apply file's note line, where a bare reference is fine.
7. **Concepts.** Define a concept in the entry only if it belongs to this entry alone. List any other concept that a reader needs in `concepts.md` in your folder: the term, the entries that use it, and where it should be defined for every worker (the `fortress-repo` core, an area part, or the short orientation that will replace the revival part). The revival part is being rewritten: do not lean on it.
8. Do not add a claim, a reason or a scope that the sources do not hold. Do not make a claim stronger or broader. Where the sources leave the meaning open, keep the current wording for that part and write a question for the curator.
9. For a fact: keep a historical measurement only if it is stated as that measurement; move repair chronology to the history; link a count that changes at every landing to the entry that owns it. A fact may record an implementation choice made at a default; say so, and never as the curator's ruling.
10. Keep each entry near 600 characters as a check, not a cap. Clarity comes first.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:

If it stays, give it a few words on what it holds, so that a reader can decide whether to follow it without loading it. If it is only provenance, move it to the apply file's note line, where a bare reference is fine.

List any other concept that a reader needs in `concepts.md` in your folder: the term, the entries that use it, and where it should be defined for every worker (the `fortress-repo` core, an area part, or the short orientation that will replace the revival part). The revival part is being rewritten: do not lean on it.
8. Do not add a claim, a reason or a scope that the sources do not hold. Do not make a claim stronger or broader. Where the sources leave the meaning open, keep the current wording for that part and write a question for the curator.
9. For a fact: keep a historical measurement only if it is stated as that measurement; move repair chronology to the history; link a count that changes at every landing to the entry that owns it. A fact may record an implementation choice made at a default; say so, and never as the curator's ruling.

An object type is a `TraitType` whose index is an `ObjectTraitIndex`, with or without static arguments, or the self type of one. ## What changed and why

The checker reads `self` as more than its trait in two kinds of trait: one whose `comprises` clause lists types (P-60; `var-ref.tex:64-69`), and one with a self-type parameter (P-146; `var-ref.tex:70-76`). It carries the reading as the type of `self`, a `TraitSelfType` with the listed types or the self-type parameter beside the trait. So `den(self)` checks for `den(r: R)` in `trait Q comprises { R }`, and `twin(self): S = self` checks in `trait Shape[\S extends Shape[\S\]\]`. On the JVM the value is typed by the trait's interface, and the verifier refuses a class that passes or returns it at the object's class.

The new member `castToTypeBelow(Expr, Type)` (`CodeGen.java:7436-7459`, directly above `conditionallyCastParameter`) emits a cast when all of these hold:

1. the declared type is a trait type or a type variable;
2. the expression's static type is self's type, a `TraitSelfType` whose list is not empty;
3. the trait does not list a type at a `where`-clause variable (`TypeAnalyzer.opensSizes`);
4. the trait is not a subtype of the declared type, and the declared type is a subtype of the trait (`TypeAnalyzer.lteq`, the general subtype test, which reads only `extends` clauses once the self type is replaced by its trait).

It is called at three kinds of place:

## What changed and why

`CodeGen.java` gets two members directly above `defaultCase` (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1800-1881`), and the runtime one class, `runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java`.

- `forLabel` (`CodeGen.java:1817`) makes a new `LabelExit.Target` for each evaluation of the block and keeps it in an immutable local under the label's name. The body is compiled in a nested scope that holds that local. An exception-table entry for `LabelExit`, written after the body's code so that the entries of a label, a `try` or an `atomic` block nested in the body come first, leads to a handler that calls `LabelExit.valueAt(target)`: it answers the exit's value where the exit names this evaluation and throws every other exit on. The value is cast to the label's type.
- `forExit` (`CodeGen.java:1862`) evaluates the `with` value, or pushes `()`, loads the target's local, and throws `LabelExit.of(value, target)`.
- `LabelExit` (`runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java:14`) is a Java `Error` that is no `FException`, without a stack trace. `LabelExit.Target` (`:19`) is an `FValue`, so that a closure holds it as it holds any immutable variable.

How an exit reaches its label from a loop's body. The body of a `for` is a function expression, and an arm of a parallel group a task; each takes the variables of the enclosing block that its body names from `FreeVariables`, in which every identifier counts (`compiler/codegen/FreeVariables.java:98`), the target of an exit among them. So the closure's class gets a field for the label's local with no change to `forFnExpr`, `delegate` or `forLetFn`. The checker lets no variable in scope share a label's name ('Cannot use an existing identifier … for a 'label' expression', `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:704`), so the name is free in the code generator's environment of locals. The exit thrown in the closure passes the library's code, and a group of forked arms joins the arms that it forked before it throws the exit on (`CodeGen.joinForkedArms`, `CodeGen.java:1681`; P-175).

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# checks.sh RUN ROUND: the record-landing workflow's mechanical checks, after a write round (ROUND 1 or 2)
# or before the commits (ROUND final, which final.sh runs).
#
# RUN is the run's folder, with run.env (prepare.sh). In the worktree, the script resets FACTS.md,
# POSITIONS.md, their histories, the gap ledger and its history to AT, the commit that the worktree was made
# at; checks the POSITIONS lines that cut-only.txt names with words-subset.py, against the reset files; then
# applies the entries writer's file with record.py apply (record.apply, or for final the judge's final.apply)
# and its row lines with ledger-clarity/apply.py (rows.rewrite, or final.rewrite); then its new rows with
# ledger.py add (rows.add; for final, final.add if the judge wrote one, else rows.add). In rows.add each
# row line, `| ? | ...`, goes in the section that the nearest `## TITLE` line above it names, a title of
# `ledger.py sections`; a row with no such line above it is not added, and the summary says so (the
# coordinator files it). The routing writer's
# edits of PLAN, PLAN-history, the review queue, INDEX and other notes stay as they are. Then it runs every
# check on the worktree: record.py check --base AT; ledger.py check; ledger.py landing-check BASE;
# check-index.sh; plan-moves.py; queue-check.py; and the length of each changed entry, lengths.py.
# record.py writes each history block "by climb batch N landing workflow (Opus)", the tier of the agents that
# wrote the text. It writes RUN/mech-ROUND.md: one line per check, pass or fail, with the PLAN lines that
# plan-moves.py lists to look at and the entries over 600 that grew (lengths.py), then each check's command
# and output.
# Exit 0 when every check passes (the length table only informs), 1 otherwise. The record files stay as
# applied, so the worktree's git diff shows the round's whole change.
set -uo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
RUN=${1:?usage: checks.sh RUN ROUND}; ROUND=${2:?round: 1, 2 or final}
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$RUN/run.env"
tools="$WT/explorations/coordinator/tools"
rec=(python3 "$tools/record.py")
led=(python3 "$tools/ledger.py")
  summary+=("- words-subset.py: no cut-only.txt, nothing to check")
fi
if [ -s "$apply" ]; then
  allp=$(mktemp -p "$WT/tmp" positions.XXXXXX); grep -E '^- P-[0-9]+ ' "$apply" > "$allp" || true
  [ -s "$allp" ] && step "words-subset.py, every POSITIONS line of $(basename "$apply")" 0 python3 "$here/../record-clarity/words-subset.py" "$allp" --root "$WT"
  rm -f "$allp"
  step "record.py apply $(basename "$apply")" 1 "${rec[@]}" apply "$apply" --by "climb batch $N landing workflow (Opus)"
else
  summary+=("- record.py apply: no $(basename "$apply"), no entry changed")
fi
if [ -s "$rows" ]; then
  d=$(mktemp -d -p "$WT/tmp" rows.XXXXXX); cp "$rows" "$d/final.rewrite"
  step "ledger-clarity/apply.py $(basename "$rows")" 1 python3 "$here/../ledger-clarity/apply.py" "$d" --root "$WT"
  rm -rf "$d"
else
  summary+=("- ledger-clarity/apply.py: no $(basename "$rows"), no row changed")
fi
if [ -s "$adds" ]; then
  d=$(mktemp -d -p "$WT/tmp" adds.XXXXXX)
  # one file per row line, row-K.txt, and d/list: K, a tab, its section ('' when no ## line is above it)
  python3 - "$adds" "$d" <<'PY'
import os, sys
sec, k, out = '', 0, []
for ln in open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'):
    t = ln.strip()
    if t.startswith('## '):
        sec = t[3:].strip()
    elif t.startswith('|'):
        k += 1
        open(os.path.join(sys.argv[2], 'row-%d.txt' % k), 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(t + '\n')
        out.append('%d\t%s' % (k, sec))
open(os.path.join(sys.argv[2], 'list'), 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(''.join(x + '\n' for x in out))
PY
  nosec=()
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r k sec; do
    if [ -z "$sec" ]; then nosec+=("$k"); continue; fi
    step "ledger.py add, row line $k of $(basename "$adds"), in \"$sec\"" 1 "${led[@]}" add "$d/row-$k.txt" --section "$sec"
    summary+=("  - $(printf '%s\n' "$last" | head -1)")
  done < "$d/list"
  [ ${#nosec[@]} -gt 0 ] && summary+=("- ledger.py add: not added, no \`## TITLE\` line above them in $(basename "$adds"): row line(s) ${nosec[*]}; file each with ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE")
  [ -s "$d/list" ] || summary+=("- ledger.py add: $(basename "$adds") holds no row line")
  rm -rf "$d"
else
  summary+=("- ledger.py add: no $(basename "$adds"), no row added")
fi
step "record.py check --base $AT" 1 "${rec[@]}" check --base "$AT"
step "ledger.py check" 1 "${led[@]}" check --summary
step "ledger.py landing-check $BASE" 1 "${led[@]}" landing-check "$BASE"
step "check-index.sh" 1 bash explorations/coordinator/check-index.sh
step "plan-moves.py" 1 python3 "$here/plan-moves.py" --root "$WT" --base "$AT"
look=$(printf '%s\n' "$last" | grep -c '^LOOK ' || true)
[ "${look:-0}" -gt 0 ] && summary+=("  - plan-moves.py lists $look PLAN lines to look at (its LOOK lines below)")
